FIX ROUND 794b for story #794 (three deadline tests flake in the host exact-coverage gate), on branch story-794-deadline-tests, already checked out in this worktree at 0feda664 (cut from main ebe818f7).

You are fixing exactly ONE more load-starved test, of the same class #794 exists for, and nothing beside it. TEST-ONLY: no production code changes. If you find the production code wrong, stop and say so in your notes, and do not fix it here.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (your diff is judged against 0feda664):
- 0feda664, story run implement-story-794-flake-effect-36657947 (review residual LOW, no security residual). It moved four effect_replay/agent_fallback seats that hang to their kill onto the engine's 30 s startup bound (tests/support/engine.rs HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS). The review found the root cause: under load, admission ran past a 1 s timeout_seconds (dispatch.rs:93-101 admits within (began, timeout_seconds) before anything spawns, and refuse_admission at broker/admission.rs:427-440 journals a plain effect/failed, so the attempt retries). It was not a slow driver start.
- When you are done, the branch is 0feda664 plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main.

THE FLAKE (measured by the controller): the host exact-coverage gate's library shard failed this test in 2 of 4 runs on 2026-10-20, at load about 6.6 and about 9, with two seat lanes running:
- `broker::session::readiness::tests::bindings_looked_up_before_a_stalled_write_still_guard_the_closure_given_up_on`, panicking at crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session/readiness/tests.rs:917:9:
  left:  ("closed", "cancelled", (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Refused(Handoff))), None)))
  right: ("closed", "cancelled", (Err(Failed(Failed(Masking))), ([], None, Some(Lifecycle))))
- Its "cancelled" leg (:908-912) cancels the attempt by the clock, `late = move || Instant::now() >= at` with `at = soon()` = now + 500 ms. The test's own comment assumes the store read, where the binding is looked up, happened long before the cancel. Under load the lookup lands after the cancel, so the handoff Closed is appended and not refused. Its "deadline" leg (:905-907) gives the startup a 500 ms deadline, and the control (:917-920) a 300 ms one. Both rest on the same assumption.
- The code under test is main's: f73ee03a, 2026-10-14, the broker's serve. `delivered` is at crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session/readiness.rs:320. Its `(end, bind)` pair, and the `given_up` and `plan_lived` helpers at readiness/tests.rs:860-884, are how the test drives it.

DELIVER:
1. Reproduce deterministically in a scratch edit, never committed: delay the store read or the binding lookup past 500 ms (for example a sleep inside the test's `bind` path or a slowed admitted store), and see the gate's exact assertion fail. Quote it.
2. Fix the test so that a slow store read cannot change what it asserts, while each leg still proves what it exists to prove:
   - the deadline leg: a startup that gives up at its deadline after the lookup still guards the closure;
   - the cancelled leg: a startup cancelled after the lookup still guards the closure;
   - the control: an unrelated binding leaves the handoff cause and its closure.

   The fix b9 (the broker's author) suggested is to cancel once the lookup is SEEN, rather than on the clock. For example, the cancellation predicate reads a flag the `bind` path sets, and the deadline leg's deadline is not reached before the lookup is seen. Separating "the lookup happened" from "the clock" is preferred over raising the 500 ms. If you raise any bound, say why it bounds the lookup and what it costs in test time.
3. Prove it: with step 1's injected delay, the fixed test passes. Record before and after in the commit message. Run the test 20 times in a loop under load (for example while `cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib` runs beside it), and report the counts.
4. The test keeps its name and its three assertions' expected values. Say what each assertion now binds.

OVERLAP TO RESPECT: PR #792 (decision 0065 slice two, U8b, in the merge queue right after #797) edits this same file at `plan_lived` (readiness/tests.rs:881): its ledger tuple becomes `(attempt, std::ffi::OsStr::new("plan"), None)`, because `lived` takes a third, staging element. Do NOT change `plan_lived`, and do not add a new call to `lived` or a new ledger tuple. Keep your change inside the test body (about :897-930) and, if you need one, a new small helper that does not call `lived`, so it rebases onto #792 without conflict. Touch no other file. In particular, not session/ production code and not tests/capability_broker/.

Gates, all clean, from the worktree root:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- broker::session:: (timeout 590)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- effect_replay:: agent_fallback:: (timeout 590)
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files and clones
- git diff --check

When a test fails, keep its whole failure text: do not filter cargo test output through grep or tail before reading it. Quote the panic message, and any cause line it prints, in your notes. Seats cannot run jscpd: if your change re-keys clones, say so, and the controller refreshes the baseline. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's: do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Commit one signed-off commit (git commit -s), message "tests: <what changed> (#794)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

PARALLEL WORK: NEVER message the-forge-b9 or any brokkr-wt-* seat.
- #753 edits brokkr-core, brokkr-store, brokkr-view and brokkr-cli fleet/, tui*, ui*;
- #697 slice B edits brokkr-runtime places/compose and brokkr-cli recipes/;
- b9's U8c will not touch readiness/tests.rs until #794 lands.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: One commit, ccc2c4a4, on 0feda664 (signed off). It is TEST-ONLY and touches only readiness/tests.rs. CAUSE: the test's own `bind` cannot carry the suggested flag, because `delivered` calls it only after `handed` has answered or given up (readiness.rs:343). So I needed another signal that the lookup had happened. The signal: the sender sets O_NONBLOCK on its dup of the control pipe only in `sent` (readiness.rs:569). It reaches `sent` only after `send_environment` has published the lookup (handoff.rs:62 found, then :64 send). A dup shares the open file's flags. FIX: new helpers. `probed()` fills the pipe with `full()`, sets the writer back to blocking with ioctl_fionbio(false), and keeps a try_clone of it as the probe. `seen(probe)` reads fcntl_getfl NONBLOCK. `after_lookup(probe)` is a predicate that never cancels but returns only once the lookup is seen (polled every 1 ms, bounded at 30 s). The cancelled leg's predicate is `|| seen(&probe)`, with its deadline 30 s away. The deadline leg keeps its 500 ms deadline and the control its 300 ms one, both with after_lookup, so the supervisor never reads the deadline as passed before the lookup. No bound was raised; the 30 s ceiling applies only if the lookup is never seen. Normal time cost: the test ran in 2.34 s before the change. After it, I measured 2.54 s with the 600 ms delay on the cancelled leg only, and 3.02 s with 600 ms on every leg. `given_up` now takes the control pipe's writer from its caller; I had to touch it outside the test body because it built the pipe internally. It adds no call to `lived` and no ledger tuple, and plan_lived is untouched. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against origin/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-792-97050d1d gave a clean tree, 24864c0c. REPRODUCTION (scratch sleep of 600 ms before `published.begin()` in delivered, never committed): with the sleep on the cancelled leg only (deadline more than 10 s away), the gate's exact failure: 'panicked at crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session/readiness/tests.rs:917:9 left: ("0002", "cancelled", (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Refused(Handoff))), None))) right: ("0002", "cancelled", (Err(Failed(Failed(Masking))), ([], None, Some(Lifecycle))))'. With the sleep on every leg, the same left at :912 for "deadline". AFTER: the test passed with 600 ms on the cancelled leg only, 600 ms on every leg, and 2000 ms on every leg (10.02 s). WHAT EACH ASSERTION BINDS (scratch mutations, all restored): M1, delivered passes Handed::Nothing to bind: fails :944, the deadline leg, left (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Refused(Handoff))), None)). M2', handed's give-up path returns Handed::Nothing only before the deadline: the deadline leg passes and :949, the cancelled leg, fails with the same left. M3, Ledger::bind latches Masking for any non-empty binding: both legs pass and :958, the control, fails: left (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Masking)), None)) right (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Refused(Handoff))), None)). M4, `seen` forced to true, with the 600 ms delay: fails :944 as before the fix, so the probe is what carries the fix. So the deadline leg binds 'given up at the deadline, after a published lookup, the binding still guards the closure'. The cancelled leg binds the same on cancellation. The control binds 'an unrelated binding, actually looked up, leaves the handoff cause and its closure'. Before the change, the control could also pass vacuously when nothing was looked up. LOAD LOOP: this seat refused a background `&`, xargs and direct execution of the test binary, so I could not run `cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib` beside it. Instead I ran the whole brokkr-cli lib suite (930 tests) 20 times at --test-threads=96 on 24 cores, 1-minute load 3.3 to 13.5 by uptime. The target test passed 20 of 20. FOLLOW-UPS, same class, not fixed here: in those 20 runs at 96 threads, broker::rpc::tests::a_server_that_takes_no_call_ends_it_and_an_ended_harness_leaves_it_begun failed 7 times. It panicked at rpc/tests.rs:1259:9 with left 'MCP server call timed out' and right 'MCP server protocol is invalid', then at :913:17 with 'called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Any { .. }'. broker::rpc::tests::delivery::a_turn_that_writes_part_of_an_answer_never_waits failed twice: delivery.rs:573:13 'slept after delivering a piece'. broker::rpc::tests::masking::standard_error_is_masked_across_reads_and_decoded_only_once_whole failed once at masking.rs:598:5, missing the final 'MCP server stderr: last [secret:DOCS_TOKEN]' line. GATES, all clean: cargo fmt --check; clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib -- broker::session:: (43 passed); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it -- effect_replay:: agent_fallback:: (11 passed); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files ('file size holds') and clones ('duplication holds'); git diff --check. The exact-coverage gate is pending (the controller's). Not pushed.

members.adversarial: Adversarial read-only review of ccc2c4a4 against 0feda664: one commit, one test file; no concrete inputs-to-wrong-output finding. Traced delayed lookup, publication, shared pipe flags, deadline expiry, cancellation, sender failure and reader/probe lifetimes. The sender publishes before sent sets NONBLOCK, so the probe cannot announce lookup early. The deadline predicate waits for that signal and never cancels; cancellation follows the same signal. Expected masking/invalid-lifecycle assertions and the unrelated-binding handoff closure are unchanged. Decision 0071 ruling 9: reviewed implement notes recording delayed-read before/after failures, distinct compiling removal controls, and 20/20 target passes under concurrent lib-suite load. The existing given_up helper also changes to accept the probed writer; implement notes explain this necessary plumbing. It adds no lived call or ledger tuple; plan_lived is untouched. Independently ran the exact target (1 passed), broker::session:: suite (43 passed), cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check against base, all clean. No tracked files changed and no commits made. Exact coverage remains the controller gate.

The mechanism checks out against production: send_environment publishes the lookup before send (handoff.rs:62-64); sent sets O_NONBLOCK at entry (readiness.rs:569), the only place the control pipe becomes non-blocking, so seen(probe) — a try_clone sharing the open file description — flips exactly when the lookup is published; probed clears the flag first so seen starts false. The load-ordering claim holds because timely_at (readiness.rs:113-115) uses non-short-circuiting &: the cancel predicate is consulted on every poll even past the deadline, and polled_with reads the clock before the predicate blocks, so no give-up is finalized before the lookup is seen. Each leg still proves its purpose: the deadline leg gives up at its deadline (after_lookup never cancels) only after the lookup; the cancelled leg cancels exactly once the lookup is seen; the control's unrelated binding leaves Refused(Handoff) with the ledger closed. No bound was raised: 500 ms/300 ms kept, and the 30 s predicate patience matches the engine's 30 s startup bound and is documented. The recorded reproduction (600 ms injected delay; exact panic text at tests.rs:917:9 and :912) is in the commit message with before/after; as a read-only reviewer I could not inject a delay into the tracked file and relied on that record plus the mechanism trace. result.notes: Chief verdict for fix round 794b: clean. The panel reported clean from all three positions (adversarial, correctness, glm) and nothing in their notes addressed the gate or argued a result; the floor is clean and my own read raises it nowhere. I read the whole 0feda664..ccc2c4a4 diff: one commit, one file, crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session/readiness/tests.rs (+51/-18). I confirmed the mechanism against production rather than taking it from the panel: secret::send_environment (brokkr-protocol/src/secret/handoff.rs) calls found(bindings), which is Published::publish under the slot mutex, before send(&frame); send is linux::sent (readiness.rs:564-577), whose first act is ioctl_fionbio(pipe, true) on the sender's try_clone of the control writer, so O_NONBLOCK on the shared open file description flips only after the lookup is published; probed() clears the flag that full() set and dups the writer, so seen(probe) starts false and reads that flag by fcntl_getfl. The supervisor (handed, readiness.rs:420-449) polls with timely_at, whose non-short-circuiting & calls the test's predicate on every turn, so in the deadline leg and the control (after_lookup, never cancelling, blocking until seen or 30 s) no give-up can be finalized before the lookup is published, and in the cancelled leg (|| seen(&probe)) the cancellation is the lookup's publication itself; published.taken(false) then yields Published, which is what each leg asserts guards the closure (masking cause, ledger unclosed, Invalid::Lifecycle) and what the control asserts an unrelated binding leaves (Refused(Handoff), Closed appended). No deadlock: the predicate blocks the supervisor thread, the lookup runs on the sender thread. Test name and all three expected tuples unchanged; no bound raised (500 ms, 500 ms, 300 ms kept; the 30 s predicate patience is documented and degrades to a loud failure, never a false pass). given_up gained only the writer parameter at its three call sites; plan_lived (:875-884) and its ledger tuple untouched and outside both hunks, no new lived call, no new ledger tuple, so it rebases onto #792. No production, frozen or other file touched. Decision 0071: ruling 9 holds (the before/after reproduction with a 600 ms injected delay, exact panic text at :917:9 and :912, is recorded in the commit message, and removing publish-before-send or take-after-give-up in production would fail each leg loudly); rulings 4, 5, 6 hold (three tiny helpers, no clone re-keyed per quality/ratchet.sh clones). Gates I ran at the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; git diff --check 0feda664..HEAD clean; typos --hidden clean; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones hold; cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked broker::session:: 43 passed, 0 failed, 5.02 s, including the target. The glm member independently ran the workspace clippy and the effect_replay/agent_fallback it suite (11/11) and 20/20 target runs beside a looping brokkr-runtime lib suite. Observations carried unrated, not returned: (1) the lookup signal is sent's ioctl, which no test pins directly (the_intent_is_sent... hands sent a pipe full() already made non-blocking), so a sent that stopped setting O_NONBLOCK would make this test slow-pass at 30 s a leg rather than fail; the shape is pre-existing, since the cancelled leg always had a 30 s far deadline as its escape. (2) The exact-coverage gate remains the controller's and is pending. I changed no tracked file and made no commit.
